subject: science
passage: A cuttlefish can change the color and pattern of its body in less than a second, matching sand, rock, or seaweed closely enough to vanish from view. Layered over light-reflecting cells and packed with millions of tiny elastic sacs of pigment called chromatophores, ______ Because each sac is stretched open or squeezed shut by muscles wired directly to the brain, a new pattern can ripple across the animal almost instantly.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: muscles turn the cuttlefish's skin into a kind of living display screen.
choices.B: scientists have compared the cuttlefish's skin to a kind of living display screen.
choices.C: the cuttlefish's skin works as a kind of living display screen.
choices.D: the cuttlefish uses its skin as a kind of living display screen.

explanation.why: The modifier "Layered over light-reflecting cells and packed with millions of tiny elastic sacs of pigment" describes a tissue, not the whole animal: it is the skin that lies over reflecting cells and holds the pigment sacs. So the noun right after the comma must be the skin.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The subject "muscles" comes right after the modifier, so the sentence says the muscles are packed with pigment sacs.
explanation.B: Incorrect. Placing "scientists" right after the modifier says the scientists are packed with pigment sacs, so the modifier dangles.
explanation.C: Correct. The subject "the cuttlefish's skin" comes right after the modifier, so it is the skin that is layered over reflecting cells and packed with pigment sacs.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Placing "the cuttlefish" right after the modifier says the whole animal is layered over light-reflecting cells; the modifier describes its skin.
